sections.heading: Teach me what I cannot see on my own
sections.text: Holy Spirit, God, teach me what I do not yet know and what I cannot understand by myself. Keep me humble as a student of Jesus. Show me the truth about myself without excuses: that apart from your mercy I am fallen, sinful, and deserving of judgment. Do not let me forget how deeply I need a Savior. Keep before me the truth that without Christ I am empty-handed and powerless to live before you.
theological_themes: The Holy Spirit teaches believers and keeps them humble before Christ.
True self-knowledge includes honest conviction of sin and dependence on Christ alone.

scripture_references.connection: Jesus teaches that fruitfulness and spiritual life depend on abiding in him; this directly supports the prayer’s confession that apart from Christ I can do nothing.

Paul describes the human condition apart from grace as spiritually dead and under wrath, then shows that salvation comes by God’s mercy. This grounds the prayer’s sober self-knowledge and need for a Savior.

sections.heading: Open Scripture and show me Christ
sections.text: Open my mind to understand your Word. As I read Scripture, help me see what you have revealed about the Father, the Son, and the Spirit. Bring light into the dark places of my mind so that I truly know Jesus—not just facts about him, but the saving knowledge of who he is and what he has done.
theological_themes: The Spirit illumines Scripture and leads believers into the knowledge of Christ.
Saving knowledge is not merely information but Spirit-given understanding of Jesus revealed in the Bible.

scripture_references.connection: The risen Christ opens his disciples’ minds to understand the Scriptures, showing that true understanding of God’s Word is a gift from God.
Paul says the Spirit reveals what God has freely given, which supports asking the Spirit to make the truths of Scripture and salvation known to the heart.

sections.heading: Help me rest in what Christ has finished
sections.text: Show me more clearly how Jesus carried out everything he came to do for sinners. Help me trust his completed work instead of leaning on my own efforts, feelings, or record. As I rest in him, let me know the Father’s love in the Son—the Father of Jesus made my Father too. By your work in me, draw me into real fellowship with the Father, the Son, and you, the one true God.
theological_themes: Christ’s saving work is complete and sufficient for believers.
Through the Son and by the Spirit, believers have access to the Father and fellowship with the triune God.

scripture_references.connection: Hebrews presents Christ’s one sacrifice as finished and effective, grounding the prayer’s desire to rest on his completed work rather than personal performance.
This passage describes access to the Father through Christ in one Spirit, closely matching the prayer’s Trinitarian movement into fellowship with God.
After his resurrection, Jesus speaks of his Father as also the Father of his disciples, supporting the prayer’s confidence that the Father of the Son has become my Father in Christ.

sections.heading: Make the Father’s love real to my heart
sections.text: Spirit of wisdom and revelation, lead me into the truth I need for peace with God. Make the Father’s love more than an idea to me; press it into my heart through the Scriptures. Apply the blood of Christ to my conscience again and again, so that I believe, with real comfort, that his blood cleanses me from every sin.
theological_themes: The Spirit assures believers of the Father’s love through the gospel revealed in Scripture.
Christ’s blood cleanses sin and comforts the conscience of those who trust him.

scripture_references.connection: Paul connects peace with God through justification to the love of God poured into believers’ hearts by the Holy Spirit, fitting this prayer for inward assurance of the Father’s love.
John teaches that the blood of Jesus cleanses from all sin, directly supporting the prayer’s plea for the Spirit to apply Christ’s cleansing work to the conscience.
Paul prays for the Spirit of wisdom and revelation so believers may know God more deeply, which aligns with asking the Spirit to lead into truth and peace.

sections.heading: Keep me coming to the Father with confidence
sections.text: Lead me on from faith to deeper faith. Give me freedom to come to my reconciled Father at all times. When doubts, fears, sinful desires, or temptations push against my peace with him, help me stand on what Christ has done. Teach me to draw near to Jesus with a clean heart, convinced of his love, and with steady confidence in him. Do not let me turn back or lose my footing on this way.
theological_themes: The Spirit strengthens faith and gives believers confidence to draw near to God through Christ.
Assurance must be guarded against doubts, fears, corruption, and temptation by resting in Christ’s finished work.

scripture_references.connection: Hebrews calls believers to draw near with confidence because of Jesus’ blood and priestly work, matching the prayer’s desire for a clean conscience and full assurance of faith.
Paul teaches that the Spirit bears witness to believers’ adoption and enables them to cry to God as Father, supporting the prayer for free access to a reconciled Father.
This passage names the ongoing conflict with sinful desires and calls believers to walk by the Spirit, which fits the prayer’s request for help against corruptions and temptations.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The original’s statement that the sinner is 'justly deserving everlasting destruction' is intentionally strong and reflects historic Protestant teaching on sin and judgment; it has been preserved rather than softened.

The phrase 'covenant undertakings' reflects Reformed covenant theology, especially Christ’s saving mission and fulfillment of God’s redemptive purposes. This can be expressed in broadly biblical terms, though some theological systems define the covenantal framework differently.

The language of the Spirit applying Christ’s blood 'effectually, continually' was rendered as the Spirit pressing Christ’s cleansing work into the conscience repeatedly; this avoids implying that Christ’s sacrifice is repeated, while preserving the original’s concern for ongoing assurance.
significant_interpretive_choices: I treated the prayer as addressed specifically to the Holy Spirit, while retaining its Trinitarian shape: the Spirit teaches Christ’s work and brings the believer to the Father through the Son.

I rendered 'learning daily there what I am in myself' as honest self-knowledge apart from mercy, rather than as a denial of the believer’s new identity in Christ. The original is emphasizing dependence, not saying the Christian remains unchanged by grace.
I interpreted 'the things that belong unto my peace' as the gospel truths that establish peace with God and assure the conscience, rather than as general emotional calm.
